verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; one confirmed UB (uninitialized scalar) repaired; no open STOP
scope: mechanism-contract sweep over attribution ranks 101-108 (unattributed-site ranking). Six ordinary files audited; two BIO callback files deferred to a BOUNDARY batch. Repairs in src/property/parse.rs, src/pem/pem_lib.rs, src/x509/x509_acert.rs, src/ssl/ssl_ciph.rs and a contract clarification in src/x509/pcy_tree.rs.
contracts_reused: OB-1 OwnedBuf plain/cleansed adoption at authority coordinates (property definitions, AttDataBuf, SSL_CIPHER_description scratch block)
Module-local PemBuf / OwnedDer owners with authority release sites (pem_lib reader and writer buffers)
OwnedTree / OwnedLevels / OwnedNode policy-graph ownership, with tree_levels/level_ptr as the only level-address arithmetic
ASN.1 item layout and getter/borrow contracts (x509_acert static templates and accessors; x509_att stack helpers)

defects.description: ossl_parse_query's '-name' override arm assigned oper/optional/name_idx but never type_. stack_to_property_list and ossl_property_merge copy the definition as a whole, and ossl_property_list_to_string forms a reference to it, so an uninitialized scalar was read even though every current consumer tests oper before the union. This is UB independent of whether a reader currently observes the field.
defects.fix: Both parsers now write a fully initialized definition (definition_zeroed()) into each fresh CRYPTO_malloc block immediately after adoption. The value is all-zero, i.e. type_ == OSSL_PROPERTY_TYPE_STRING, oper == OSSL_PROPERTY_OPER_EQ, name_idx == 0, v == 0; the parsers' existing per-field assignments overwrite the fields they name. A focused assertion pins the override clause's type_.
defects.witness: property::parse 7/0, including a_query_records_negation_override_and_optionality now asserting the override clause's initialized type. No in-tree reader observes a behaviour change; the authority leaves the field unset, so deterministic zero is a documented divergence on an unobservable path.

defects.description: PEM_def_callback stored strlen(userdata) in a c_int and passed the truncated value to memcpy. A NUL-terminated string longer than INT_MAX (C-valid input) or a negative num made the size argument enormous, so the copy wrote out of bounds. The authority has the same signed truncation.
defects.fix: Compute the length as size_t, clamp it to max(num, 0), copy that many bytes, and return the same c_int. For every valid (num >= 0, length <= INT_MAX) the result is byte-identical to the authority.
defects.witness: pem::pem_lib 2/0: def_callback_copies_at_most_num_bytes and def_callback_clamps_a_negative_length (the latter would have attempted an enormous memcpy before the fix).

defects.description: PEM_do_header checked only *plen > INT_MAX; a negative *plen was converted to c_int and passed as the input length to EVP_DecryptUpdate.
defects.fix: Reject !(0..=INT_MAX).contains(&len) before any cipher operation, raising the authority's existing PEM_LIB_459 site. All in-tree callers pass the reader's non-negative length.
defects.witness: pem::pem_lib and pem:: tests pass; no in-tree caller reaches the negative arm.

defects.description: PEM_ASN1_write_bio_internal accepted a negative return from the second i2d/i2d_ctx pass and used it as a byte count.
defects.fix: Break to the shared epilogue when the second pass answers negative, so the DER handle is clear-freed and no cipher/write call receives a negative length.
defects.witness: The focused PEM tests and the full suite pass; the authority's own failure path is the same early exit.

defects.description: c_strlen returned size_t truncated to c_int for the octet-string attribute path, and ciphersuite_cb accepted a negative len (its guard was len == 0, not len <= 0) before a copy.
defects.fix: c_strlen now returns Option<c_int> and the caller fails the attribute add when the length does not fit; ciphersuite_cb requires len > 0. CONF values and CONF_parse_list already bound those inputs, so reachable behaviour is unchanged.
defects.witness: clippy and the full suite pass; no in-module tests exist for either file.

defects.description: tree_calculate_authority_set and tree_calculate_user_set index levels[nlevel - 1] but their Safety sections said only that the tree was live. tree_init always builds n + 1 >= 2 levels.
defects.fix: Both Safety sections now state the at-least-two-level precondition established by tree_init.

residuals: src/property/parse.rs: the authority leaves an override clause's type field unset; the candidate now writes a deterministic zero. Every reader in list.rs/query.rs/parse.rs tests oper before touching type, so no observable behaviour differs, but no authority differential was run.
src/ssl/bio_ssl.rs and src/runtime/bio/bss_bio.rs were not inspected at all; their BIO callback/method boundaries are deferred rather than declared clean.
src/x509/pcy_tree.rs, src/x509/x509_acert.rs, src/ssl/ssl_ciph.rs and src/x509/x509_att.rs have no in-module unit tests; their assurance rests on the full library suite and contract review.
src/x509/x509_att.rs X509at_get_attr_by_OBJ uses lastpos + 1 (a contract-invalid INT_MAX input would panic in debug / wrap in release, not cause UB); left as authority-parity.

boundary_control.reason: M11-D1 is an initialization/aliasing invariant and M11-D2 is a length conversion; both were repaired and covered by focused tests, but the campaign's Miri and ASan negative controls for these specific paths belong to the BOUNDARY batch.
